chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Miskan, from Abi al-Abbas, from Zakariya ibn Malik al-Ja'fi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked:

about the words of God, the Exalted: 'And know that out of all the booty that ye may acquire (in war), a fifth share is assigned to God, and to the Apostle, and to near relatives, orphans, the needy, and the way-farer.'

He (peace be upon him) said: As for the one-fifth share of God, the Exalted, it is for the Prophet, who may spend it wherever he wishes. And as for the one-fifth share of the Prophet, it is for his close relatives. And the one-fifth share of the near relatives, they are his close relatives. And the orphans are the orphans of his Household. So he assigned these four shares to them. And as for the poor and the way-farers, you know that we do not eat charity, and it is not permissible for us, so it is for the poor and the way-farers.

key_terms.خُمُسُ الرَّسُولِ: The one-fifth share of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: Who receives the five shares of Khums according to Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Khisal elucidates the distribution of Khums by distinguishing between the Prophet's discretionary share and the specific entitlements of the Ahl al-Bayt, including orphans and close relatives from their lineage. It highlights the theological principle that the Imams do not consume general alms (Sadaqah), thereby reserving the shares for the poor and way-farers for the broader community. This distinction underscores the unique status of the Imams as both recipients of divine wealth and distributors of charity.
